counterfactual_missing_items: A transbronchial lung biopsy showed no malignancy or specific inflammation
pupils were equal and reactive; eyelids were not droopy
decisive_items: dense infiltrates in the ventral subpleural regions of the right upper and middle lobes
severe sweating confined to his right arm and thoracic area
decreased surface temperature over the right arm and right thorax corresponding to dermatomes C5–T12
response.rationale: R2 best integrates the right upper/middle-lobe infiltrates with the ipsilateral C5–T12 autonomic syndrome (sweating, cooling) and pleuritic pain; the negative biopsy and absent Horner's are the main counter-evidence. R6 shares the autonomic signs but lacks trauma and does not explain the lung infiltrates. R1 and R3 are undermined by antibiotic failure and no organisms; R5 is excluded by intact pupils and hyperhidrosis; R4 lacks sicca and the unilateral autonomic pattern.

rejected.why: Lung abscess is undermined by no microorganisms, no response to antibiotics, and it does not explain the localized autonomic sweating.
Horner's syndrome is contradicted by equal/reactive pupils and non-droopy eyelids; the patient has hyperhidrosis, not anhidrosis.
Sjögren's syndrome lacks sicca and does not explain the unilateral autonomic syndrome or pleuritic pain.
Empyema is contradicted by antibiotic failure and no organisms/purulent collection; the pleural rub is nonspecific.
